neighbours.label: ' high' as a noun-forming attributive modifier (high street, high-rise, high speed, high school), vs ' high' as a predicate or adverb
fire: Several shops on the high street closed during the winter.
She grew up in a high-rise block on the edge of the city.
The train runs on a new high speed line between the two cities.
My brother teaches history at the local high school.
They sell high-end watches to tourists at the airport.
The office tower is the tallest high-rise in the region.
Every room in the cottage now has high speed broadband.
The factory only makes high quality steel for bridges.
quiet: Several shops in the town were closed and the rent was high.
She grew up in a block where the walls were very high.
The train climbs until the line is high above the river.
My brother says the fees at the school are too high.
Prices for watches at the airport are always high.
The office tower rises high over the old warehouses.
In the cottage the ceilings are surprisingly high.
Demand for steel was high all through the year.

predictions: Attributive 'high' before a noun reaches 0.3-0.6; predicative 'was high' and adverbial 'flew high' stay under 0.07.
notes: Card: ' high' x23 (high street, high-end, high-rise, high speed, high quality, high school). Probe: high street 0.549, high-rise 0.399, high speed 0.321; 'prices were very high' 0.061, 'flew high' 0.001, 'online retailers' 0.003; low-rise leaked 0.278 (opposite adjective in the same compound).
